subject.title: fix(llm): summarize ephemeral tool results to preserve prefix cache

question: Which tool-result visibility policy should OpenClaw use for prefix-cache providers: narrow heartbeat/session-status summarization, isolated heartbeat sessions, or broader tool-output elision?
rationale: The code can mechanically preserve provider tool-call pairing, but deciding which tool outputs may be hidden from the model affects agent reasoning, session continuity, and provider-cache behavior across real users.

options.title: Narrow content elision to proven ephemeral outputs
options.body: Keep normal `exec`, `read`, `web`, and `memory` results visible and only summarize outputs whose owner proves the model does not need the content, with live DeepSeek proof.

options.title: Prefer isolated heartbeat sessions
options.body: Avoid changing provider replay semantics and instead make heartbeat or automation runs avoid contaminating the main session context.

options.title: Pause for the canonical policy discussion
options.body: Leave this PR as exploration until the linked issue settles the tool-result lifecycle and live repro requirements.

recommendation.title: Narrow content elision to proven ephemeral outputs
recommendation.body: Keep normal `exec`, `read`, `web`, and `memory` results visible and only summarize outputs whose owner proves the model does not need the content, with live DeepSeek proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest prompt-cache transport history signal and is the best identified owner for the provider-cache policy choice.
